32 An electron moves between two points X and Y in a uniform electric field, as shown.
Y
uniform electric field
X
The distance between X and Y is 4.0 cm and the line XY is at an angle of 60° to the direction of
the field.
The field exerts the only force on the electron.
The field strength is 100 N C–1.
What is the change in the kinetic energy of the electron as it moves from X to Y?
A
– 4 eV
B
–2 eV
C
+2 eV
D
+4 eV

hints: Notice the $4.0\text{ cm}$ line XY is at $60^{\circ}$ to the field lines, so find the component of XY parallel to the $100\text{ N C}^{-1}$ field from X to Y.
Recall the force on an electron is opposite to the electric field direction, so compare that leftward force with the rightward component of motion from X to Y.
Use work done $W = Fd\cos\theta$ equals change in kinetic energy, and use $1\text{ eV}$ as the energy of charge $e$ moved through $1\text{ V}$ to avoid converting $e$.
walkthrough: Identify the displacement along the field. From the diagram motion from X to Y has a component to the right, along the field, of $d = 4.0\text{ cm} \times \cos 60^{\circ} = 2.0\text{ cm} = 0.020\text{ m}$.
State the force direction. For charge $-e$ the electric force is $F = -eE$, so it acts to the left with magnitude $e \times 100\text{ N C}^{-1}$, opposite to the rightward displacement component.

Set work equal to kinetic energy change. The field exerts the only force, so $\Delta E_k = W = Fs_{\text{parallel}}$ with sign from the angle $180^{\circ}$ between leftward force and rightward displacement.
Calculate the potential difference magnitude along the motion: $V = Ed = 100\text{ N C}^{-1} \times 0.020\text{ m} = 2.0\text{ V}$.
Apply the electron sign. Moving with a component along $E$ means moving to higher potential for a negative charge with work done negative: $W = -e \times 2.0\text{ V} = -2.0\text{ eV}$.
Hence $\Delta E_k = -2\text{ eV}$. This is option B.

A.explanation: This uses the full $4.0\text{ cm}$ along the field and the wrong sign. Only the $60^{\circ}$ component counts and the electron loses kinetic energy.

B.explanation: Work done by the field is negative because the force on the negative electron opposes the $2.0\text{ cm}$ displacement along the field, giving $-2\text{ eV}$.

C.explanation: This has the correct $2\text{ eV}$ magnitude but the wrong sign. It treats the electron as if the force were in the field direction.

D.explanation: This uses the full $4.0\text{ cm}$ with no $\cos 60^{\circ}$ factor and the wrong sign, giving $+4\text{ eV}$.
